title: Imported Cosmetics Ingredient & Labelling Review in Korea: Prohibited Ingredients, Limits, Full Ingredient Listing | YouSun Administrative Agency
h1: Ingredient and labelling review for imported cosmetics
lead: Before imported cosmetics enter Korea, the full ingredient list should be checked against the lists of ingredients that cannot be used and ingredients with use limits, and the Korean-language packaging must carry the required particulars in the required manner. The cosmetics responsible seller (화장품책임판매업자) reports the ingredient list before distribution and sale and prepares and keeps an import management record.
summary: Who: cosmetics responsible sellers importing cosmetics manufactured abroad for distribution and sale in Korea.

Filed with: the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS, 식품의약품안전처) for the ingredient list report (before distribution and sale; may be omitted when importing with a standard customs clearance pre-report filed as an electronic trade document), and the regional MFDS office (지방식품의약품안전청) that requested substantiation data for labelling and advertising (where the relevant report or application is filed).

Key checks: prohibited ingredients, use limits for preservatives, UV filters and hair dye ingredients, Korean-language particulars and full ingredient listing, fragrance allergens and precautions for use.

Deadlines: ingredient list before distribution and sale; substantiation data within 15 days of the request; the result of an application to designate or change an ingredient use standard is notified within 180 days of submission.
Our scope: document review of ingredient lists and label drafts, and preparing documents filed with the authorities (no testing or analysis, no customs import declarations).

sections.h2: What does an ingredient and labelling review for imported cosmetics cover?
sections.body:
Three things. (1) Ingredients: that the product contains no ingredient MFDS has designated as one that cannot be used, and that ingredients requiring use restrictions, such as preservatives, colourants and UV filters, stay within their limits. (2) Labelling: that the primary and secondary packaging carry the statutory particulars in clear Korean and list all ingredients in the prescribed manner. (3) Labelling and advertising claims: that no wording could make the product be mistaken for a medicine or a functional cosmetic, and that factual claims can be substantiated.

No one may sell cosmetics that use a prohibited ingredient, or import, store or display them for sale; a violation can lead to imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. Cosmetics that breach the labelling rules also may not be sold, stored or displayed for sale. It is therefore safer to align the formula and the label draft before shipment.

sections.h2: What is checked when comparing the full ingredient list before import?
sections.body:
The specification and content data for each ingredient obtained from the manufacturer are compared with the two lists in the Regulation on Cosmetics Safety Standards (화장품 안전기준 등에 관한 규정).

(1) Ingredients that cannot be used: for example, lead and its compounds, mercury and its compounds, hydroquinone and antibiotics are on this list. If any is present, the formula for the Korean market must be changed.

(2) Ingredients requiring use restrictions and their limits: for preservatives, phenoxyethanol is limited to 1.0%, and parabens (p-hydroxybenzoic acid, its salts and esters, excluding phenylparaben) to 0.4% as a single ingredient and 0.8% in mixtures (as acid). For UV filters, zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are each limited to 25%; the hair dye ingredient p-phenylenediamine may be used up to 2.0% in oxidative hair dyes and not in other products. Preservatives, UV filters and similar ingredients not on this list cannot be used.

To use an ingredient without a designated use standard, an application can be made to designate one, and the result is notified within 180 days of submission (or of submitting supplementary data, if requested). Animal testing is also checked: a cosmetics responsible seller may in principle not distribute or sell cosmetics that were animal-tested or made or imported using animal-tested ingredients.

sections.h2: What must appear on cosmetics packaging?
sections.body:
The outer packaging shows (1) the name of the cosmetic (2) the business name and address (3) all ingredients used in manufacture (4) volume or weight of contents (5) the batch number (6) the expiry date or period after opening (7) the price (8) for functional cosmetics, the words 'functional cosmetics' (기능성화장품) or the designated mark, and (9) precautions for use. Where secondary packaging is added, the primary packaging shows the name, business name, batch number and expiry date or period after opening (cosmetic soap is exempt from primary-packaging labelling).

Also required are a barcode; where an ingredient name is used in the product name, that ingredient and its content (except fragrance products); and, if the product is labelled or advertised specifically for infants or children, the content of preservatives. For imported cosmetics, the name of the country of manufacture (may be omitted if the country of origin is shown under the Foreign Trade Act), the manufacturer's name and its address are shown, distinguished from the domestic cosmetics manufacturer.

All particulars must be placed where they are easier to see than other text, in accurate and easy-to-read Korean; Chinese characters or foreign languages may be added. Breaching the labelling particulars (other than price) is subject to a fine of up to KRW 2 million.

sections.h2: How must the full ingredient list be shown?
sections.body:
(1) The font size is 5 points or more. (2) Ingredients are listed in descending order of content, but ingredients at 1 percent or less, fragrances and colourants may be listed in any order. (3) For a blended raw material, each individual ingredient is named. (4) In colour make-up, eye make-up, hair dye or nail products where colourants differ by shade, all colourants may be listed together after '± or +/-'. (5) Fragrance may be shown as 'fragrance' (향료), but if it contains a designated allergen, that ingredient must be named. (6) pH-adjusting ingredients may be shown as their neutralisation products, and saponified ingredients as their saponification products.

Ingredient names must be the standardised generic names. Rather than translating the names on the overseas label, each one is matched to the Korean standardised generic name; for an ingredient without a standardised generic name, the name should be settled before the label draft is finalised.

sections.h2: How is labelling reduced for small-volume products and samples?
sections.body:
Packaging of cosmetics with contents of 10 millilitres or 10 grams or less, and of samples manufactured or imported so that consumers can try them rather than for sale, may show only the name, the business name of the cosmetics responsible seller, the price (for samples, a mark such as 'sample' or 'not for sale'), the batch number, and the expiry date or period after opening (with the manufacturing date where the period after opening is shown).

Products over 10 millilitres (grams) and up to 50 millilitres (grams) may list, instead of all ingredients, only tar colours, gold leaf, the type of phosphates in shampoos and rinses, fruit acids (AHA), the ingredients giving a functional cosmetic its efficacy, and ingredients with a published use limit. Where ingredients are omitted, the packaging must give a phone number or website where all ingredients can be checked at once, or a booklet listing all ingredients must always be kept at the point of sale.

External feminine washes and eyelash permanent wave products are excluded from this simplification.

sections.h2: How are precautions for use and advertising wording reviewed?
sections.body:
For all cosmetics, the common precautions are: (1) consult a specialist if red spots, swelling, itching or similar symptoms appear from direct sunlight during or after use (2) avoid use on areas with wounds (3) keep out of reach of children and away from direct sunlight; wording published for each product type and ingredient is added. Twenty-five fragrance allergens are designated, and each must be named when present above 0.01% in rinse-off products or above 0.001% in leave-on products.

Labelling and advertising must not suggest the product is a medicine, make a non-functional cosmetic look like a functional one, use AI-generated sounds, images or videos that are hard to tell from reality to make it appear that doctors, pharmacists or other experts recommend or use the product, or otherwise mislead consumers. Wording that makes a foreign product look domestic (or the reverse), claims technical partnerships with foreign firms that do not exist, or uses exclusive absolute terms such as 'the best' or 'the finest' is also prohibited. Violations are subject to imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 10 million.

Factual claims must be capable of substantiation; when the regional MFDS office requests substantiation data, it must be submitted within 15 days of the request. Substantiation data include human application test data, in-vitro test data or survey data of an equivalent or higher level. Functional claims such as whitening, wrinkle improvement or UV protection require a functional cosmetics review or report first.

sections.h2: How are the ingredient list report and the import management record prepared?
sections.body:
The cosmetics responsible seller reports the list of ingredients used in manufacture to MFDS before the cosmetics are distributed or sold, and reports again when the list changes. The previous year's production or import performance is reported by the end of February each year through a cosmetics industry association such as the Korea Cosmetic Association (대한화장품협회), including the Korea Pharmaceutical Traders Association (한국의약품수출입협회). When importing with a standard customs clearance pre-report filed as an electronic trade document, the import performance and ingredient list reports may be omitted. Failing to report the ingredient list and similar items is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 1 million.

An import management record is prepared and kept for imported cosmetics. Its items are (1) product name or the name for sale in Korea (2) specifications and content of ingredients (3) country of manufacture, manufacturer's name and address (4) a copy of the functional cosmetics review result notice (5) a certificate of manufacture and sale (6) a sample product description written in Korean (7) date of first import (customs clearance date) (8) import date and quantity by batch number (9) quality test date and result by batch number and (10) buyers, sale dates and quantities. The certificate of manufacture and sale may be omitted where the import requirement confirmation body confirms the product is the same as one imported by a seller holding the certificate and a test report from a designated body's quality test is kept.

sections.h2: How far can an administrative agent help?
sections.body:
Under a letter of authorisation, YouSun Administrative Agency compares the full ingredient data of products to be imported with the lists of prohibited and restricted ingredients on paper, reviews Korean label drafts and precaution wording, checks advertising wording, prepares ingredient list reports and substantiation submission documents, prepares and files applications to designate or change an ingredient use standard, and responds to requests for supplementation.

Testing and analysis of ingredient content and human application tests are carried out by testing bodies, and customs import declarations are handled by licensed customs brokers, so we do not take these on. We also do not take on court or administrative appeal cases. Functional efficacy claims are followed up through the functional cosmetics review or report procedure. Whether a label complies and any disposition are decided by the competent authority.

faq.q: If an ingredient name is part of the product name, what else must be shown?
faq.a: The packaging must show that ingredient's name and its content. Fragrance products are excluded.

faq.q: What extra preparation is needed to label a product for infants or children?
faq.a: The packaging must show the content of preservatives with designated use standards, and the cosmetics responsible seller must prepare and keep product safety data in advance. Infants are aged 3 or under, and children are aged 4 to 13.

faq.q: Can the deadline for submitting substantiation data be extended?
faq.a: Yes, if a justifiable reason is accepted. If the data are not submitted in time and the same labelling or advertising continues, an order to stop it will be issued until the data are submitted.

faq.q: How are batch numbers and expiry dates shown on a set of several products?
faq.a: The outer packaging of a set may show each component's batch number or a combined batch number. For the expiry date, only the earliest-expiring component's date is shown, and the others can be referred to with wording such as 'Expiry date: shown on each product'.

faq.q: Can a confidential ingredient be shown as 'other ingredients'?
faq.a: Where listing an ingredient would seriously harm the business's legitimate interests, supporting data are submitted to MFDS, and if accepted, the ingredient may be shown as 'other ingredients' (기타 성분). Until then, all ingredients must be listed.

faq.q: Can an AI-generated video of an expert recommending the product be used in advertising?
faq.a: No. Advertising that uses AI-generated sounds, images or videos that are hard to tell from reality to make it appear that doctors, pharmacists, professors or other experts recommend or use the product is prohibited.
